key_insight: A lightweight CNN with transfer learning can detect multiple cancer types from MRI and CT images with high accuracy while keeping compute costs low.
clinical_relevance: This approach may support faster, more deployable image-based cancer screening in settings with limited hardware resources.
method: Trained a computationally efficient CNN on brain MRI, lung CT, and kidney CT datasets.
Used transfer learning by pretraining on one cancer type and fine-tuning on the others.
Evaluated performance with 5-fold stratified cross-validation and compared against common pretrained models.
evidence_signal: Reported test accuracy of 90.85 ± 2.22% for brain, 98.64 ± 2.43% for lung, and 99.92 ± 0.08% for kidney cancer classification across 5-fold CV.
watch_item: Results come from dataset-specific evaluations, so broader real-world performance may depend on external validation across different scanners, sites, and patient populations.
paper_title: Multi-cancer detection using a computationally efficient CNN with transfer learning
